title: aidd status --json
description: The open work: each Spec, Intent, and proposal with its stored status and its next step, then what is past due. A new optional key may be added in a minor release; a renamed or removed key bumps `schema_version`.

schema_version.description: The version of this output's shape.

root_blocker.description: Present only when open work exists and no open step is a person's: the line `aidd status` ends with. It names each item that Specs wait behind and how many, with the move that frees them and the choice, such as `SPEC-1 blocks 23 Specs: finish it, or choose a Spec to specify.` Or it names the ring of items that wait on each other. A script that shows what waits on a person shows this line when the list is empty.

items.description: The open work items, started first, then urgent ones, then by id.

path.description: The item's file, relative to the repository's top.

status.description: The status the item's front matter stores, or an Intent's status from its slices.

group.description: The status group, from the schemas' `x-groups`.

progress.description: An Intent's slices: how many finished (merged or ended), of how many.

parent.description: The Intent a Spec names as its `parent`.

stage.description: For a Spec: the stage it stands in, a name in `loop.stages` of `schemas/roles.json`, from its stored status, its Tasks' `done`, and its observe window. Absent for a cancelled Spec.

phases.description: For an Intent: its phases, in order, by their ids (a person reads each as "Phase <n> · <name>", by its place), each with its slices, their status (`planned` for a slice with no Spec file yet), and once started, their stage.

finished_on.description: The day a person recorded the phase finished.

status.description: Its Spec's status, `done` for a slice its line records as merged, or `planned`.

waiting_on.description: The unfinished items it waits for: its `blocked_by`, its slice line's, and each that says it `blocks` it.

owner.description: The person driving the work, as its front matter names them.

owner_team.description: The team accountable for the work, as its front matter names it.

delivery_teams.description: With `delivery_teams` in the config: the teams whose work the item is, by the rule `--delivery-team` uses (an Intent of the team, a Spec under one, a Spec whose `owner_team` names the team, or a Spec whose Task scope touches the team's areas).

blockers.description: The Spec's `blockers` text, as written: the wait a person must clear.

tasks.description: A Spec's Tasks, each with its state: `todo`, `blocked` (it waits for another Task or for Spec approval), `stopped` (it used its retries, so a person re-plans it), or `done`.

why.description: Why the Task is blocked or stopped.

emergency.description: The Spec's `emergency` object: the incident an emergency change repairs.

evidence.description: A summary of the worktree's last `aidd test` run, set on the one Spec the branch's diff holds. It is for a person to read and is never evidence: the runner's exit code on the head is.

commit.description: The short sha of the commit the run tested.

head.description: The short sha of the branch's head now.

behind.description: How many commits the head is past the tested commit. Absent when the head is the tested commit, or the tested commit is not an ancestor of the head.

result.description: The verdict `aidd test` exits on; `partial` for a `--changed` run or a dirty tree.

at.description: When the run wrote its evidence, in UTC (`2026-11-05T03:24:47Z`).

unsaved.description: Set on the item this worktree's branch is for, such as SPEC-1 on `spec/SPEC-1`, when the worktree holds changes in no commit yet. Removing the worktree loses that work, so the next step is to commit it on that branch.

count.description: How many paths hold uncommitted changes, new files too.

paths.description: The first of them, as git names them.

places.description: With --all-branches: the places that hold this version of the item, `worktree:<path>` or `branch:<name>`. Two places that hold different versions give two items.

history.description: With an id: the item's history, newest first, then the documents it links. Its decisions and reports from the records (the agent's account, never a yes), the commits on HEAD whose message names its id, and its `docs`. It never changes the next step.

at.description: When, in UTC (`2026-11-05T03:24:47Z`); empty for a document.

what.description: One line: the action and the question with its outcome, what was reported, a commit's subject, or a document's type and path.

ref.description: The record's id, the commit's short sha, or the document's path.

trace.description: With one work item's id, a Spec or an Intent: what stands behind it, as `aidd status <path>` gives a path.

due.description: What is past due: a feature flag past its `cleanup_due`, a deprecation past its sunset.

path.description: The work item that names it.

what.description: What is due, in a sentence.

handoff.description: Where the work on this branch stopped, from the handoff note in its last commit's message, when no Spec the branch is for holds a note: a change with no Spec before its PR/MR. Only on a branch of one's own. It is the agent's account, never a yes.

commit.description: The short sha of the commit whose message holds the note.

explorations.description: Present only when an exploration's `status` is `open`: a person owes its pick, so a person has a step. Each gives its file, its question, the work item whose folder holds it, and the step.

path.description: The exploration's file, relative to the repository's top.

question.description: The question the exploration answers, as its front matter writes it.

item.description: The id of the work item whose folder holds it; absent for one under `specs/explore/`.

unreadable.description: A work item whose front matter does not parse, with the reason: still open work, which `aidd validate` names in full.

place.description: With --all-branches: the place that holds the file.

delivery_teams.description: With `delivery_teams` in the config: the team names, in the config's order, so a team with no open work still has its lane.

next.description: With nothing open: what to do next.

step.description: A next step: its stable code, who takes it, and what it is.

code.description: A stable code, such as `spec.approval`, that a script may match on.

who.description: Who takes the step: an agent, a person, or nobody, when the step waits on other work or the work is finished.

person.description: For a step a person takes: who answers. The first approver for an approval, else the owner.

words.description: What a person types to their agent, or the command to run, to take the step. Absent for a step nobody takes, and for an item whose id is not a plain id (the schema's id pattern), because words hold no other text of the repository.

why.description: Why the step comes next, in one line, read from the data that owns the reason: the loop's lanes and decision rights in `schemas/roles.json`, or a schema's meaning. Absent where no data owns one, such as finished work.
